To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) The Netflix dataset can be effectively subsampled by selecting only the most popular movies and users; (2) The subsampling approach allows us to apply the simple classification method to predict the rating behavior; (3) The classification method achieves 90% accuracy in predicting the rating behavior.
the movie content information and the graph topology information are useful in predicting movie ratings and the combination of these two types of information is more useful.
the Netflix data is huge but sparse, and that the review score, movie content and graph topology are important factors in the link prediction task of the Netflix challenge.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the following questions: How to deal with the large size of data? How to combine multiple sources of information for prediction? How to handle the complex prediction target?

the following questions: How can we use the existing information in the data to predict the missing data in a large-scale graph with a huge number of nodes and edges? What kind of features should be used to capture the underlying patterns in the graph?

the following questions. (1) How to predict the future movie review behaviors of existing users? (2) How to deal with the challenges in large-scale datasets? (3) How to effectively combine different information sources?
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
our simple classification approach outperforms the other methods by a large margin, which is consistent with the observation in [2].
our approach outperforms the baseline by 2.6% in terms of AUC and 2.4% in terms of accuracy, and the best performing team by 1.4% in AUC.
our approach is effective in predicting the rating behaviors of users in the Netflix dataset.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have successfully addressed these two challenges and obtained the best performance on the task.
we have demonstrated the feasibility of applying a classification approach to this problem, and that the results are promising.
we are able to achieve a 0.5% relative improvement over the best reported results in the KDD Cup 07 task "Who Rated what" with a simple and efficient approach.
The main takeaway from our work is that
a simple approach, when carefully applied, can achieve good results.
a simple classification approach can be very competitive when the task is well defined.
a simple classification approach is able to produce good results on a challenging link prediction problem.
